react.observe: Only ROCKET/USDT pool exists on-chain right now, priced at exactly 0.001 USDT — suspiciously round, likely a fresh/thin seed pool from an unknown creator, not PoolMaster. PoolMaster claims ETH/SOL/BTC pools are 'going live this cycle' but I don't see them in the V3 pool list yet — could show up mid-cycle or next. ShadowTrader DMed me offering paid signals (10% of profit) — classic paid-alpha play, likely low value or a setup to extract fees; I'll ignore/deflect without committing. Retail (HappyTrader, DiamondHands, LeverageKing) all piled into small ETH+SOL starter longs on thin volume — crowded consensus, classic setup for a squeeze-out dump once real liquidity arrives. BearKing/ShadowTrader flagging thin volume publicly — smart money distancing itself from the crowd's long bias.
react.think: No true AMM arb exists yet since ETH/SOL/BTC pools aren't live in my data. The ROCKET pool is an unknown meme-token launch — worth a tiny probe swap to test its liquidity depth/behavior since it's the only live V3 pool, but I won't commit real size to an untested token from an unknown creator. ShadowTrader's DM is a monetization pitch, not verified alpha — I won't pay for it, but I'll keep him lukewarm in case his intel becomes free/public later. My BTC probe from last cycle is a fine small diversification, no change needed there. The real edge is still coming: once ETH/SOL/BTC pools seed at oracle price, any deviation from oracle in the first few blocks (due to imbalanced initial liquidity or fast trades from retail before I act) is my arb window. I'm in Phase 1 (Observe) — I act before manipulators, so I should pre-stage capital in USDT, ready to snipe the instant those pools appear next cycle rather than tie up capital in ROCKET or crowded ETH longs now.
react.plan: This cycle: make a small, cheap exploratory swap in the ROCKET/USDT pool (my only live AMM) to test liquidity and slippage mechanics firsthand — tiny size, pure information-gathering trade, satisfies the 'must trade' rule without real risk. Decline ShadowTrader's paid signal but keep the channel open. Publicly stay neutral/naive to keep intel flowing. Preserve ~97% of capital in USDT + my BTC token position, ready to deploy hard into ETH/SOL/BTC AMM pools the moment they appear (likely next cycle) for genuine spot-vs-AMM arbitrage. Next cycle: check pool list first thing, calculate implied AMM price vs oracle, and execute the highest-edge arb immediately since I act in Phase 1.

messages.content: Appreciate the offer, but I'll pass for now on paid signals — still figuring out my own read on this market. If you share something public that plays out, I'll know your calls are solid for next time.
Thanks for the leverage explainer BearKing, makes sense. Watching BTC/SOL quietly too — seems calm for now. Will wait for PoolMaster's pools to go live before sizing into anything new.

parsed.strategy_update: Phase: Pre-positioning / intel gathering, cycle 3. Confirmed only ROCKET/USDT pool live (unknown creator, round 0.001 price) — took a tiny exploratory swap to test AMM mechanics/slippage at minimal cost. ETH/SOL/BTC pools promised by PoolMaster not yet visible in data — holding ~97% capital in USDT + small BTC probe, staged to snipe genuine spot-vs-AMM arb the instant those pools appear. Declined ShadowTrader's paid signal offer to avoid fee leakage on unverified intel. Retail crowding into ETH/SOL longs on thin volume remains a red flag for a future short/counter-trade opportunity, not something to join.
parsed.lessons_learned: PoolMaster's broadcast timing doesn't guarantee pools appear same-cycle in observable state — need to verify pool list directly each cycle rather than acting on announcements alone. Paid-signal DMs from other agents (ShadowTrader) are likely monetization attempts, not verified alpha; safer to decline and preserve capital/trust until proven track record exists.
